one-place.title: Check 1: Several notes, one place
one-place.question: Where must 5 go in this row?
one-place.reason: The row needs a 5, and neither column 2 nor column 7 allows it. Column 5 still lists 2 as a candidate, but placing 2 there would leave no place for 5 in the row. Place 5, then check the affected groups again. This does not settle the order of 2 and 7 in the two remaining cells.

two-places.title: Check 2: A similar row, a different conclusion
two-places.question: Can the same check tell you where to place 5 now?
two-places.answer: Not yet: 5 can go in column 2 or column 5.
two-places.reason: Column 2 now also allows 5. Having fewer candidates in column 5 does not make that cell the answer. This row snapshot permits both placements of 5, so this check alone cannot choose between them. On a full board, look for another justified move and return to this row afterward.
